articles.excerpt: Disclosure: This draft was generated with AI and checked against the cited primary sources, with a separate AI editorial review. It was prepared for the FrameSprite team, which has a commercial intere…
articles.body: Disclosure: This draft was generated with AI and checked against the cited primary sources, with a separate AI editorial review. It was prepared for the FrameSprite team, which has a commercial interest in FrameSprite. Proposed examples are not executed tests unless explicitly identified as recorded fixture results. HaxeFlixel may reuse cached image data when several sprites load the same graphic. Editing that shared pixel data can therefore alter more than one enemy. Request a unique graphic for an instance that owns destructive pixel edits, or keep the effect in per-sprite rendering state. See the bitmap cache API . Key Takeaways Shared artwork is useful until an instance needs to mutate it. Decide whether damage paint belongs in source pixels or in a visual effect.

articles.title: Filux: Self-Hosted File Sharing with Docker or Native Linux
articles.excerpt: Sending one large file should not require creating another cloud account. Nor should collecting a document from a client mean asking them to email six compressed attachments. A small self-hosted file-…
articles.body: Sending one large file should not require creating another cloud account. Nor should collecting a document from a client mean asking them to email six compressed attachments. A small self-hosted file-sharing service can handle both jobs: you upload a file, send an expiring link, or give somebody a private upload link that drops files into a folder you choose. That is the appeal of Filux , an open-source file storage and sharing application released under the AGPL. Its clean interface, controlled public shares, and Request Files workflow cover the most common file-transfer jobs without another subscription. This guide covers both Docker Compose and native Linux installations, with HTTPS, restricted network access, and a backup plan.

articles.excerpt: Disclosure: This draft was generated with AI and checked against the cited primary sources, with a separate AI editorial review. It was prepared for the FrameSprite team, which has a commercial intere…
articles.body: Disclosure: This draft was generated with AI and checked against the cited primary sources, with a separate AI editorial review. It was prepared for the FrameSprite team, which has a commercial interest in FrameSprite. Proposed examples are not executed tests unless explicitly identified as recorded fixture results. Resizing a HaxeFlixel graphic and resizing its collision box are separate decisions. setGraphicSize changes scale; updateHitbox then changes collision dimensions and offset and recenters the origin. Calling it after designing a smaller collider can undo that design. These operations are documented in the FlxSprite API . Key Takeaways Decide whether a resize should change gameplay collision. Apply custom collision dimensions after automatic hitbox updates.

articles.title: What Happens When AI Gets Its Own Computer?
articles.excerpt: How Sandboxes Help AI Agents Work Safely Have you ever wondered what would happen if an AI could control a computer instead of just answering questions? Imagine asking an AI to write code, run command…
articles.body: How Sandboxes Help AI Agents Work Safely Have you ever wondered what would happen if an AI could control a computer instead of just answering questions? Imagine asking an AI to write code, run commands, and test an application automatically. Sounds amazing, right? But what if it accidentally deleted an important file or ran a dangerous command? That is where sandboxing becomes important. What Is an AI Sandbox? A sandbox is an isolated environment where software can run without having unrestricted access to the main system. Think of it like a separate room where an AI agent can perform its tasks without freely accessing everything in your house. For example, a developer can run an AI-generated script inside a Docker container instead of running it directly on their main computer.

articles.title: Sub-50 ms Is Not a Voice-Agent SLO: Build a Turn Budget and Overload Envelope
articles.excerpt: Sub-50 ms Is Not a Voice-Agent SLO: Build a Turn Budget and Overload Envelope A voice-AI demo can report a 42 millisecond model response and still make a caller wait three seconds. It can start speaki…
articles.body: Sub-50 ms Is Not a Voice-Agent SLO: Build a Turn Budget and Overload Envelope A voice-AI demo can report a 42 millisecond model response and still make a caller wait three seconds. It can start speaking quickly and still interrupt a hesitant customer. It can pass a laboratory latency test and fail during the first Monday-morning traffic spike. The number is not necessarily false; it is incomplete. Production voice systems are pipelines. Audio capture, endpoint detection, transport, speech recognition, dialogue state, retrieval, tools, model inference, safety policy, speech synthesis, jitter buffers, and telephony all consume time. Some work overlaps, some runs sequentially, and some happens only on difficult turns. A component benchmark therefore cannot serve as the service promise.

articles.title: Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter?
articles.excerpt: A Russian satellite just conducted a startlingly close approach of a private American Earth-observing satellite. What was the goal of the controversial maneuver?
articles.body: A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit. A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

articles.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
articles.excerpt: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered inter…
articles.body: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales. The sticking points Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not.

articles.body: In Avengers: Infinity War , when Dr. Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) and a variety of other heroes are awaiting Thanos’ arrival on Titan, Strange uses the Time Stone to look into alternate futures to see the possible results of the impending conflict. Star Lord (Chris Pratt) asks Strange how many futures he looked into, and Strange replies, “14,000,605.” Then Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.) asks how many of those resulted in their victory. Strange, looking deep into Stark’s eyes, says, “One.”
